spec.name: suggestion-sorting
spec.intent:
Census @25f9e3a1 (the source tree; the design records amending notebook, architect role and planner role were written after it and reach this plan's line with its bind). Every path is repo-relative on the plan's line. A line number, size or count below is a measurement at 25f9e3a1: re-derive it if its path changed since. Add no test file beyond what the acceptance names. Realize `architect role` as amended at its newest version: the architect sorts what the operator says into what must hold, which (once rectified) goes into the design, and suggestions about how a concept might be built, which never do. It captures each suggestion at once, as it is said, as an idea note whose topic is that concept; and when it cuts that concept into a shard for the planner it hands those notes WITH the shard, by title, never inside it. The shard stays what and why and never how, so the assayer, which judges a unit against its shard, never judges against a suggestion. Everything else in the gloss is already realized (the route clauses, plan-closed, route-names, ad hoc dispatch) and stays as it is.

HOME. The contract is the `architect` Role value, packages/canon/src/dimensions/role/architect.ts (3530 bytes at 25f9e3a1). Its reads and writes already carry `note`. Extend the two clauses this changes, in the value's own notation: `rectify(input)` (the operator's input is sorted: what must hold ↦ C after rectification; a how-suggestion ↦ an idea note captured at once, its topic the concept, ¬ C), and `cut(C)` (the shard ↦ planner, with the idea notes on that concept handed beside it, ¬ inside it). packages/canon/src/roles/architect.ts: the description and the archetype each say it in one clause where they already speak of rectifying inputs and cutting shards; update the cell comment only if it would otherwise be false.

NOT HERE. The design and note skills are not this unit's: capture already exists, and the concurrent unit resolved-notes writes both skills; this unit edits neither and binds no symbol of either (say it in the role value's own words, as the design skill's existing 'capture a decision note' line does). The personas kino, mav and nico hold this role through `holds` and inherit the change; their residue is untouched. The purview guard reads the holder's projected role section as its law and passes a dispatch to a planner; it needs no edit.

.changeset/suggestion-sorting.md: '@cratylus/canon' minor.
accept: In the `architect` value, the `rectify(input)` clause sorts the operator's input into what must hold (to C) and how-suggestions (to an idea note on that concept, never C), and the `cut(C)` clause hands the idea notes on the concept with the shard and not inside it; `grep -c idea packages/canon/src/dimensions/role/architect.ts` prints at least 1 (0 at 25f9e3a1).
`grep -c -i suggest packages/canon/src/roles/architect.ts` prints at least 1 (0 at 25f9e3a1), the hits in the description and the archetype.
`git diff <the commit the unit's work starts from> --name-only` lists only this unit's outputs.

In packages/canon, `pnpm exec vitest run test/reader-density.test.ts test/persona.test.ts test/purview-guardrail.test.ts test/symbols.test.ts test/symbol-altitude.test.ts test/symbol-probe-gate.test.ts` exits 0 (the RESIDUE gate admits only σ* anchors in a dimension value) and `pnpm --filter @cratylus/canon typecheck` exits 0.
